messages:
Alex: Quick brain-dump — we need a concrete proposal for the policy-decider service that routes requests by customer tier + region and triggers model-variant fallbacks when latency/availability SLOs are at risk. Thinking: per-tenant tier config (p99 latency target, avail target), region-aware health, and a short-circuit 'safety valve' that swaps to cheaper/compact model variants.
Maria: +1. Console UX: we need to show the active policy, what triggered a fallback, and a manual override toggle per customer. keep it simple for Support. :eyes:
Kevin: For API, propose a single decision endpoint: POST /decide with body {customer_id, region, model_requested, recent_metrics_summary}. Decision response: {route: HOSTED|DEDICATED|PRIVATE, model_variant, reason_code}. Example payload inlined below.
Kevin: ```
{
  "customer_id": "acct_123",
  "region": "eu-west-1",
  "model_requested": "gptx-13b",
  "metrics": {"p50": 40, "p95": 120, "p99": 260, "error_rate": 0.004} // ms and fraction
}
```
Sophie: Observability requirements: we need telemetry labels: customer_tier, region, model_variant, fallback_reason, decision_latency_ms. Also histograms for decision latency and gauge for active_fallback_count. Add an event stream for fallback occurrences.
Alex: On thresholds: recommend tier definitions like gold (p99 <= 150ms, avail >= 99.95%), silver (p99 <= 300ms, avail >= 99.9%), bronze (p99 <= 600ms, avail >= 99.5%). These are placeholders, open to tweaking.
Maria: UX should expose those SLOs and the last triggered timestamp. Also a small timeline of fallback events per customer (last 7 days) and the chosen variant each time. Support should be able to revert a forced fallback.
Kevin: Implementation detail: policy rules should be evaluated in this order — 1) region capacity check, 2) tenant p99 vs target (sliding window 5m/20m), 3) error-rate spike, 4) model-specific health (out-of-memory / queue depth). If any rule fails, return a fallback decision.
Sophie: For detection windows, prefer sliding-window percentiles over simple leaky-bucket for latency. For availability, use a rolling error-rate with exponential decay weighting so bursts matter but we avoid flip-flopping.
Alex: Good. Also include KV cache hits: if prefix cache hit rate high we can keep higher-capacity model even if latency near threshold. Add cache_boost flag to decision.
Kevin: Schema tweak: response includes "fallback_reason" with codes: CACHE_HIT, LATENCY_SLO, AVAILABILITY_SLO, REGION_OVERLOAD, MODEL_CRASH. Consumers can surface friendly messages.
infra-bot: deploy ci/policy-decider v0.9.1 started by @kevin — build 8421 — staging -> canaries
Maria: One security note — per-tenant overrides must be RBAC-gated and audited. Add an audit log entry every time a manual override is used.
Sophie: Telemetry naming convention proposal: redwood.policy_decision.count, redwood.policy_decision.latency_ms_bucket, redwood.policy_fallbacks.total with labels {tier, region, model_variant, reason}.
Alex: Open questions: do we allow cross-region fallback (route to another region) for gold customers? That impacts data residency. I'd default to no for regulated tenants and make it configurable per account.
Kevin: Action items: 1) I'll draft API spec + example responses (owner: Kevin, due EOD tomorrow). 2) Maria drafts console wire for fallback timeline and override (owner: Maria, due Wed). 3) Sophie publishes telemetry spec + dashboard template (owner: Sophie, due Fri). 4) Alex to write policy operator DSL proposal for complex rule composition (owner: Alex, due next Mon).
Maria: tiny UX nit — show the last decision_reason inline on per-request traces so Support can triage immediately.
Alex: 👍 I'm happy with this direction. We'll review Kevin's API draft in the eng-platform sync. Thanks all.
